body:
Heavy-lane check (independent gate-runner, release, head 735c9106) - **this PR stays a draft: one fixture that plans on main now falls back.**

All heavy tests pass, but the new geometry budget fires at five places. Four of them were already refused on main by the #13 work budget at the same levels (the PR only refuses sooner: `rotary_adaptive` developed window 86 -> 53-55 revolutions; motion `pocket3d_hsm` stepped block Z -10: 180 -> 92; `adaptive_hsm` island 60x40: 163 -> 88).

The fifth is new: app `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` - on the PR one level is refused after 19 revolutions at ~515 k vertices and cut by Offset rings; on main the same run shows no refusal (grep for "refused" in its output is empty). The test passes either way, so it hides the change of toolpath for that level. Test time 234 s on main vs 130 s on the PR.

So the 500 k calibration cuts a plan that finishes today. Owed before this can be ready: measure the bore's vertex totals per level, recalibrate (or change the unit so a finely tessellated outline is not penalised per vertex) so that every fixture that plans on main - heavy lanes included - still plans, and make the bore test assert that no level falls back so it cannot hide this again.

Quick pass (orchestrating session): the rework is pushed (head e8def282; the last commit touches only the decisions file, the tested code is ecb54b7f); merges cleanly with main; the author's quick gate and clippy were green, and this time the author ran all 13 heavy adaptive lanes in release on that code - all pass. Flagged ready for the full review. The regression the first cut had is gone: the user's STEP bore gives the same toolpath on main and on this PR (5530 moves, digest a91f154b99d44f62), and the bore test now asserts no budget refusal. The rule changed from a raw vertex budget to 'more than 600 k vertices AND more than 5,000 tool radii of walk' (both deterministic). Island: 52.6 s -> 22.0 s in release. This is toolpath-planner code under the safety floor: a high-tier review is owed before merge. Follow-up #882 filed for the bore's own 200 s of planning.
